LESSON: CONDITIONS FOR SWALAH

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Devotional Acts
Topic 4.1.3: Conditions for Swalah

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Conditions for Swalah. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. state the conditions for swalah as a requirement for its validity
2. demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CONDITIONS FOR SWALAH
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Conditions for Swalah helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: CONDITIONS FOR SWALAH
Study Conditions for Swalah like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: State the conditions for swalah as a requirement for its validity

What this means
In this part you learn to state the conditions for swalah as a requirement for its validity. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: state the conditions for swalah as a requirement for its validity.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Conditions for Swalah” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can state the conditions for swalah as a requirement for its validity. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Conditions for Swalah in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Conditions for Swalah is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Conditions for Swalah” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: state the conditions for swalah as a requirement for its validity)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Conditions for Swalah in your own words. (skill: demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Conditions for Swalah to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: state the conditions for swalah as a requirement for its validity.
3. Practise this skill: demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Conditions for Swalah from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Conditions for Swalah: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Conditions for Swalah?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Conditions for Swalah means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: state the conditions for swalah as a requirement for its validity.
5. Be able to: demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
